trips.title: Grüner Veltliner and the Wachau Terraces
trips.sub: Wachau, Lower Austria
trips.summary: A week on the Danube terraces tasting Grüner Veltliner and Riesling by classification, from walk-in cooperatives to email-only growers.

trips.title: Lambic, Geuze and the Trappist Table
trips.sub: Pajottenland, Zenne Valley and Brussels
trips.summary: A week between Brussels tables and the Zenne valley's wild-fermenting lambic cellars, with one long day into Trappist country.

trips.title: Mavrud and the Broad-Leaved Vine: Thrace to Melnik in Harvest Week
trips.sub: Thracian Lowlands PGI and the Struma Valley PGI
trips.summary: Bulgaria makes wine from grapes that grow nowhere else and are named after the places that kept them. Mavrud is dark, tannic and stubborn on the plain below Plovdiv; the broad-leaved Melnik vine will only ripen in…

trips.title: Istria in Truffle Season: Motovun Forest, Malvazija & the World's Best Oil
trips.sub: Central Istria, the Mirna valley & the west coast
trips.summary: Istria in autumn is the only place in Europe where the white truffle, world-class olive oil and a serious indigenous white grape occupy the same forty kilometres. You base inland among the hill villages, Motovun on its 277 m cone, Grožnjan, Buzet, hunt Tuber magnatum in the oak and poplar woods of the Mirna floodplain, and eat it grated over fuži by the gram. Between truffle days you work through Malvazija Istarska and Teran, taste down a Flos Olei shortlist, meet boškarin ox, and finish at Rovinj with Kvarner scampi. No drive exceeds an hour.

trips.title: Moravian Cellars and Bohemian Lager
trips.sub: South Moravia, Plzeň Region and Prague
trips.summary: A week from Prague's beer halls to Pilsner Urquell's cellars and on to Moravia's VOC wine villages and cliffside sklepy lanes.

trips.title: Champagne, Chalk to Cork
trips.sub: Reims, Épernay, Côte des Blancs and Côte des Bar
trips.summary: A week from Reims' Roman chalk cellars to Épernay's Avenue de Champagne and the grower villages of the Côte des Blancs and Côte des Bar.

trips.title: The Côte d'Or, Climat by Climat
trips.sub: Côte de Nuits and Côte de Beaune, Burgundy
trips.summary: A week walking the Côte d'Or's Grand Cru and Premier Cru climats, from Beaune's covered market to domaines that answer email in weeks, not days.

trips.title: Baden Wine and the Black Forest Table
trips.sub: Kaiserstuhl and Ortenau, Baden-Württemberg
trips.summary: A week on Germany's warmest wine hills, from Kaiserstuhl cooperatives and Ortenau growers to the Black Forest kitchen and Freiburg's daily market.

trips.title: Riesling on the Mosel Slate
trips.sub: Mittelmosel, Rhineland-Palatinate
trips.summary: A week on the Mosel's blue-slate slopes, tasting Riesling by Prädikat and Grosse Lage from cooperative doors to appointment-only cellars.

trips.title: Crete End to End: Horta, Graviera & the Raki Fires
trips.sub: Chania, Rethymno, Heraklion & Lasithi
trips.summary: Crete's food identity is older than the mainland's: a Minoan-rooted diet of wild greens, barley rusk, sheep's cheese and raw olive oil that epidemiologists spent the 1960s writing down. The week runs west to east, Chania's covered market, Rethymno's mountain villages, Heraklion's PDO wine zones, then the Lasithi olive country around Sitia. You eat dakos most days, learn six wild greens by leaf, and drink Vidiano and Liatiko from grapes grown nowhere else. In late autumn the island smells of pomace: raki distilling is a licensed communal event you can be invited to.

trips.title: Bull's Blood and Noble Rot: Seven Days Between Eger and Tokaj
trips.sub: Eger and the Bükk foothills, then Tokaj-Hegyalja on the Bodrog
trips.summary: Two Hungarian wine regions, three hours apart, that share almost nothing. Eger is rhyolite tuff, Kékfrankos, and a horseshoe of cellar doors cut into a valley wall where you drink standing up. Tokaj is loess over…

trips.title: West Cork Larder: Ballymaloe to Skibbereen
trips.sub: County Cork, East Cork, Kinsale and West Cork
trips.summary: A seven-day culinary & wine tour itinerary in County Cork, East Cork, Kinsale and West Cork, Ireland.

trips.title: Sangiovese Spine: Chianti Classico, Montalcino & the Pecorino Hills
trips.sub: Chianti Classico, Montalcino, Val d'Orcia & Cortona
trips.summary: One grape, three denominations, and a 90 km transect explaining why they taste nothing alike. You start on the galestro ridges between Greve and Radda, where Chianti Classico has just redrawn itself into eleven named sub-zones; drop south to Montalcino, where Sangiovese Grosso ripens earlier and spends five years in wood; and finish among Pienza's pecorino dairies and Cortona's Etruscan terraces. Three estates a day is a hangover, two is an education. It suits people who want to leave able to taste Panzano against Lamole blind.

trips.title: Vilnius & Aukštaitija: Farmhouse Ale and Mead Road
trips.sub: Vilnius, Aukštaitija (northeast Lithuania), Biržai, Dzūkija
trips.summary: A seven-day culinary & wine tour itinerary in Vilnius, Aukštaitija (northeast Lithuania), Biržai, Dzūkija, Lithuania.

trips.title: Crémant and the Luxembourg Moselle
trips.sub: Moselle Luxembourgeoise
trips.summary: A week along the Route du Vin tasting Crémant de Luxembourg, Riesling and Elbling from cooperative caves to appointment-only biodynamic growers.

trips.title: Underground Streets and Feteasca Neagră: A Week Through Codru and Ștefan Vodă
trips.sub: Chișinău, the Codru hills, Ștefan Vodă and the southern Valul lui Traian
trips.summary: Moldova is the only wine country where you tour two of the cellars by car, windows down, headlights on, past street signs that read *Cabernet* and *Feteasca*. Above ground it is quieter than that sounds: low Codru…

trips.title: Cheese, Genever and the North Holland Table
trips.sub: North Holland and the Schiedam distilleries
trips.summary: A week from Amsterdam's brown cafés to Alkmaar's cheese-carrier guild and Schiedam's tall malt-mill distilleries, timed to the new herring season.

trips.title: Vranec & Stanušina: The Tikveš Basin and the Vardar Road
trips.sub: Tikveš & Povardarie, Kavadarci, Negotino, Demir Kapija, Štip & Skopje
trips.summary: Tikveš is the largest continuous vineyard region in the Balkans and almost nobody visits it. The basin sits between the Vardar and the Kožuf mountains, gets around 270 sunny days a year, and grows Vranec, the black, tannic national grape, alongside Stanušina, a pale indigenous red found nowhere else. The week runs south from Skopje through Negotino, Kavadarci and Demir Kapija, staying in wineries that built their own rooms because there were no hotels, then east to Štip for pastrmajlija. Come in September and the whole country is outdoors making ajvar over open fires.

trips.title: Solaris and Smoked Plums: A Małopolska Eating and Drinking Week from Kraków
trips.sub: Małopolska, Podhale & the Carpathian Foothills
trips.summary: Poland has 500-plus registered vineyards and almost nobody outside the country has drunk one. This week runs from a Kraków bread ring you eat standing up, through a hillside vineyard below a monastery where the monks…

trips.title: Douro Field Blends: Quintas, Tawnies & the Pocinho Line
trips.sub: Alto Douro Vinhateiro, Baixo Corgo, Cima Corgo & Douro Superior
trips.summary: The Douro is a landscape argument: pre-phylloxera field blends of forty varieties planted together on schist terraces so steep the region needed UNESCO protection to justify farming them at all. The week runs upriver from the softer, wetter Baixo Corgo through the Cima Corgo heartland at Pinhão to the near-desert Douro Superior, learning the port hierarchy, ruby, LBV, tawny, colheita, vintage, before circling back to Vila Nova de Gaia to see where those casks actually age. Dry Douro DOC reds are now half the story and get equal time. Trains, a rabelo leg and a driver day mean nobody has to stay sober on the switchbacks.

trips.title: Fetească and Fire Water: A Week Through Dealu Mare and Drăgășani
trips.sub: Dealu Mare (Prahova & Buzău), the Buzău Land Geopark, and Drăgășani on the Olt
trips.summary: Romania makes more wine than New Zealand and Austria combined and almost nobody outside it drinks any. This week fixes that: a sun-facing terrace of Carpathian foothill vineyard where Fetească Neagră ripens like a…

trips.title: Veltlínske and Furmint: The Small Carpathian Wine Route and Slovakia's Secret Tokaj
trips.sub: Malokarpatská vinohradnícka oblasť and the Slovak Tokaj
trips.summary: Twenty minutes by train from Bratislava the vines start and do not stop for forty kilometres. This is the Malokarpatská route: Grüner Veltliner from limestone slopes, a Slovak-bred white nobody outside the country…

trips.title: Burja Country: Vipava's Zelen, Karst Teran & the Osmica Trail
trips.sub: Vipava Valley, the Karst & eastern Goriška Brda
trips.summary: Two adjoining regions divided by a wind and a rock. The Vipava Valley is flysch and green terraces growing two white grapes that exist almost nowhere else, Zelen and Pinela, under the burja funnelling off the Trnovo plateau. Twenty minutes south the Karst is red terra rossa over limestone, where the same wind cures pršut in unheated lofts and Teran is defined by acidity. Between them sits the osmica, a farm licensed to sell its own wine and meat for eight days at a time, announced by an ivy branch on a pole. The week is built to catch two.

trips.title: The Sherry Triangle: Solera, Tabanco & the Bajo de Guía
trips.sub: Marco de Jerez, Jerez de la Frontera, El Puerto de Santa María, Sanlúcar de Barrameda & Cádiz
trips.summary: Three towns, twenty kilometres apart, producing wines that cannot legally be made in each other's cellars. You spend the week learning why: albariza chalk, the flor yeast veil, the fractional blending of the solera, and the sea humidity that makes Sanlúcar's manzanilla thinner and saltier than Jerez's fino from identical grapes. Between visits it is a tapas trip, tabancos where a copa costs €1.60, Cádiz's Mercado Central, langostinos at the Guadalquivir mouth, retinto beef from the Vejer marshes. Cheap for what it is, and the most technically interesting wine week in Spain.

trips.title: Skåne Wine Country: Österlen & Kullabygden
trips.sub: Skåne, Österlen, Kullahalvön and the Malmö-Lund axis
trips.summary: A seven-day culinary & wine tour itinerary in Skåne, Österlen, Kullahalvön and the Malmö-Lund axis, Sweden.

trips.title: Fendant, Raclette and the Valais Vineyard Trail
trips.sub: Valais, between Sion and Sierre
trips.summary: A week between Sion and Sierre on Switzerland's driest, sunniest wine slope, tasting Fendant and native reds and following the historic irrigation bisses.
